analysis.problem_summary: Reverse an array of characters in-place using O(1) extra memory.
analysis.intuition: To reverse a sequence in-place, the outermost elements must swap positions, followed by the second outermost elements, moving progressively toward the middle.
approach: Initialize two pointers: `i` at index 0 (start) and `j` at index `s.length - 1` (end).
Iterate while the left pointer `i` has not passed the right pointer `j`.
Swap the characters at `s[i]` and `s[j]` using a temporary variable `temp`.
Increment `i` and decrement `j` to move both pointers toward the middle.
analysis.why_it_works: Swapping the elements at index `i` and `j` exchanges the $i$-th element from the front with the $i$-th element from the back. Repeating this until the pointers meet effectively mirrors the entire array.
analysis.key_takeaway: Using two converging pointers is the optimal strategy for in-place array reversal, achieving O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
analysis.time_explanation: The loop performs $n/2$ iterations, where $n$ is the length of the string array `s`. Each iteration performs constant-time swap operations, resulting in an overall time complexity of $O(n)$.
analysis.space_explanation: All operations modify the input array directly in-place, using only a constant amount of extra memory for two pointer indices and one temporary character variable.
